title: CloudPipe — Pipeline Throughput
description: How many subjects went through the pipeline, how many finished, how long they took, and how long they waited for a node. One row per Argo workflow.

options.content:
### 🚚 Is work getting through the pipeline?

One **workflow** = one participant taken through the whole pipeline. A participant reprocessed after a failure has several workflows, and every attempt is counted here — that is deliberate, since throughput is about attempts, not about distinct people.

**Waiting vs. running.** Queue wait is time spent with nowhere to run, before any processing starts: the cluster scales nodes on demand, so a burst of submissions waits for machines to boot.

🚨 **Averages here only count workflows that have FINISHED.** While a batch is running they describe the workflows that finished first — the short ones — not the batch. Check **n** and **Minutes since last finish** before quoting any average: near-zero minutes means the number is provisional and biased low. Leg 1 (true mean 3.68h) read **1.15h** three hours in and **6.28h** at nine hours before settling.

⚠️ Workflows are dated by when they **finished**, while the QC dashboards date records by when the workflow **started**. A batch running past midnight UTC therefore lands on different days across dashboards. When comparing eras, filter on `started_at`, not `dt` — the pre-leg-1 test batches (through 2026-08-18T16:54Z) finished on dates that overlap leg 1.

panels.title: Workflows run

targets.rawSQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_runs FROM cloudpipe_metrics.workflow_runs WHERE from_iso8601_timestamp(started_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE)

panels.description: Every attempt in range, including reprocessing. Not a count of distinct participants.

panels.title: Finished successfully

targets.rawSQL: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'Succeeded' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS success_pct FROM cloudpipe_metrics.workflow_runs WHERE from_iso8601_timestamp(started_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE)

panels.description: Share of workflows ending in Succeeded. A partial outcome (some sessions processed, others not) does not count as success here.

panels.title: Mean time to finish

targets.rawSQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(total_duration_s) / 3600.0, 2) AS mean_hours, COUNT(*) AS workflows FROM cloudpipe_metrics.workflow_runs WHERE from_iso8601_timestamp(started_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE)

panels.description: Mean wall-clock duration over ALL terminal workflows in range — successes and failures alike, because a workflow that ran 12h before being deadline-killed occupied a slot for 12h. Read the n beside it: this average is over COMPLETED workflows only, so while a batch is still running it reflects whichever workflows have finished so far, not the batch. That sample is length-biased — short workflows finish first. Replaying leg 1 (final mean 3.68h over n=2978), this panel would have read 1.15h at 3h elapsed, 6.28h at 9h, and only settled near 3.68h once the batch drained. Trust it when 'Minutes since last finish' is large; treat it as provisional when that is near zero.

panels.title: Mean wait for a node
panels.description: Time between submission and the first pod actually starting — cluster scale-up latency, not processing time. Consistently high values mean the node pools are the bottleneck, not the pipeline.

targets.rawSQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(pending_duration_s) / 60.0, 1) AS mean_queue_min FROM cloudpipe_metrics.workflow_runs WHERE from_iso8601_timestamp(started_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE) AND pending_duration_s IS NOT NULL

panels.title: How workflows ended

targets.rawSQL: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS count FROM cloudpipe_metrics.workflow_runs WHERE from_iso8601_timestamp(started_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE) GROUP BY status ORDER BY count DESC

panels.description: Count per terminal status. Failed and Error are distinct: Error generally means the pod was lost (evicted, node reclaimed) rather than the code failing.

panels.title: Minutes since last finish

targets.rawSQL: SELECT GREATEST(date_diff('minute', MAX(from_iso8601_timestamp(finished_at)), $__timeTo()), 0) AS mins_since_last_finish FROM cloudpipe_metrics.workflow_runs WHERE from_iso8601_timestamp(started_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE)

panels.description: Gap between the newest finish in range and the end of the window — a censoring check for the averages above, NOT a health metric. Near zero (red) means workflows were still completing when the window closed, so the batch is only partly represented and 'Mean time to finish' is a running total over whichever workflows finished first — biased short. Large (green) means the batch drained well before the window ended, so the averages are over a complete population. Leg 1 read 1886 here once settled; a live batch reads 0. Clamped at 0, which also covers a fixed past window whose workflows finished after it closed.

panels.title: Recent workflows

targets.rawSQL: SELECT subject, pipeline, status, started_at, ROUND(total_duration_s / 3600.0, 2) AS duration_h, message FROM cloudpipe_metrics.workflow_runs WHERE from_iso8601_timestamp(started_at) BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() AND CAST(dt AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE) ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 50

panels.description: Most recent first. `message` carries the failure text when there is one.
